rationale: Both candidates correctly recognize that the GT's three top-level blockers (partition-aware enabler, unrunnable offline example) and both inline bugs (missing packed_total, missing attn_backend fake) are already resolved in this diff snapshot, and both independently rediscover the deeper live issue behind GT concern #2: the engine's hardcoded rel_l1_thresh=0.2 default silently defeats the new model-specific 0.17 default, so users never get the calibrated safe threshold — a strong, well-evidenced convergent find. X adds a sophisticated, well-grounded critique of the calibration polynomial itself (near-constant, non-monotone, R²=0.09) that questions whether the adaptive mechanism functions at all, which is a first-order concern with clear prescriptive fixes; Y contributes a novel, concretely-evidenced finding that quality=high can silently activate Cache-DiT alongside TeaCache despite the docs' 'mutually exclusive' claim. Both reviews are thorough, technically deep, and heavily cite specific code locations, but X's synthesis is more prioritized/narrative and its 'what I verified' section demonstrates deeper correctness verification of the packed-multimodal contract, giving it a slight edge in actionability and coherence.
